subject: Plan alignment & bundling options for RealmHealth
messages:
From: Alice Davenport <alice.davenport@realmhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@realmhealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — bundling options and target budget

Hi Rachel and Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising for our triage workflows. Procurement asked me to get an initial read on packaging and what a typical path looks like if we:

- Start on a mid-tier Dedicated plan for 6 months
- Then either upgrade to Reserved Dedicated or move to a Private deployment by year-end depending on compliance progress

We have two internal asks: 1) can you outline the recommended feature bundles (observability, KV cache persistence, higher retention for traces) and 2) whether there are discount bands tied to committed GPU months or ARR. We also need a short timeline for migration complexity (hours/days) so our infra team can plan.

For budget planning, finance carved out ~$220k for H1 trials but procurement will push for discounts if we commit to a 12-month path. Can you share a proposal with options and an attached feature matrix? If you could loop in someone who owns Dedicated pricing that would help.

Cheers,

Alice
Head of AI Integrations
RealmHealth

Subject: Re: Initial ask — bundling options and target budget

Hi Alice — great to hear from you and glad the demo surfaced helpful numbers. Short answer: yes, we can present 3 clear price/pack options and attach a feature matrix. Longer answer below and I attached an updated pricing proposal (pricing-proposal-v2.pdf) plus a feature-matrix spreadsheet.

Quick summary of the three recommended paths:

1) Trial Mid (6 months) — Mid-tier Dedicated
   - Purpose: validate latency and throughput on real traffic
   - Bundles: Observability (90d retention), Prefix KV cache (default), Standard tracing
   - Billing: monthly usage + 20% committed capacity discount if reserve >= 2 GPU-months

2) Predictable Reserved (12 months) — Reserved Dedicated
   - Purpose: predictable unit economics for production rollout
   - Bundles: Observability (365d), KV persistence snapshotting, Advanced tracing hooks, Rollouts (canary)
   - Billing: flat monthly commit; step discounts at 12/24 GPU-months; typical 10–18% off list for 12mo

3) Private Deployment (VPC) — Enterprise license
   - Purpose: compliance and data residency
   - Bundles: All infra features + optional HSM/KMS integration and longer SLAs
   - Billing: platform license + infra run rate; discounts negotiated on ARR/term

Migration complexity (rough):
- Mid -> Reserved: low (configuration switch + capacity reservation), typical 4–8 hours ops work
- Reserved -> Private: medium (networking, certs, KMS), typical 3–5 business days with customer infra coordination

I copied Marcus who manages Dedicated pricing; Karthik will help size the initial commit recommendation if you can share an approximate QPS/profile and token distribution.

Next steps: if you confirm target QPS and whether compliance gating is required this quarter, we’ll return a redlined pricing PDF with two discount bands (6mo commit, 12mo commit) and an explicit migration checklist.

Thanks,

Rachel Kim

Hi all — quick technical clarifications to help sizing and bundling: 

- What is the expected average and 95th percentile request length (tokens)? That drives memory/KV cache footprint.
- Do you expect many long-running chat sessions or mostly single-turn inference?
- Any regional residency constraints beyond US (e.g., EU sites)?

On discounts: we typically preserve feature parity across tiers; discounts are tied to committed GPU-months and multi-year ARR. For a single-region 12mo reserved commit of ~24 GPU-months we can typically structure a 12–15% discount off list, plus a one-time onboarding credit for proof-of-concept artifacts if you sign within 30 days. If you need a larger ARR-level concession we’ll need a CX/finance approval and will outline the criteria in the redline.

Marcus — can you confirm lead times for Private deployments (networking windows + cert provisioning) and whether we can offer a trial Private sandbox?

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel and Karthik — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the attachments: 

- Procurement wants the 12-month Reserved scenario priced at both 12 GPU-months and 24 GPU-months so they can compare unit costs.
- They asked for an explicit clause on data retention change windows (we need confirmation we can extend observability retention without full migration).
- For Private deployment, they want a firm estimate of network runbook tasks (number of windows, cert rotation steps).

We can share a sample token histogram and request size distribution early next week (Mon/Tue). Can you add a short paragraph in the proposal that clarifies rollback/fallback if we hit performance regressions during rollout? That made procurement more comfortable with an initial 6-month trial.

If possible, could you flag which features in the matrix are "add-on" vs "included" for each tier — procurement wants that as a one-page summary.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can get the redline and the two commit bands by Tuesday EOD that would put us on track for February procurement approval.

Best,

Alice

RealmHealth
